name: Watson Looks Down at the Street
description: Watson walks to the window, reaches up, and pulls the curtain aside. He peers down at the street below, watching the movement beneath.
related_events: Watson peers down at the street from behind the curtain

name: Watson Jogs Down a Deserted Street in Anger
description: Watson, his face set in fury, jogs down the center of a deserted street. He carries a cane in one hand and opera glasses in the other, a flower still tucked behind his ear. His strides are quick and determined, echoing faintly in the empty space around him.
related_events: Watson jogs down the center of a deserted street in an enraged state

name: Bus Arrives on Rainy Street with Umbrella-Held Passengers
description: Rain falls steadily on the city street. A bus approaches, its open-top deck filled with passengers holding umbrellas. The umbrellas cluster together, dark and rounded, resembling black mushrooms sprouting above the vehicle as it moves through the wet afternoon.
related_events: Bus arrives on rainy street with passengers using umbrellas

name: Cabbie Arrives and Rings Doorbell
description: The cabbie steps onto the pavement, pulls out a piece of paper, and checks the address written on it. He looks up at the house number, then walks to the door and presses the doorbell.
related_events: Cabbie arrives at house and checks address
Cabbie rings doorbell

name: Holmes Examines Cardboard with Green Smudges
description: Holmes stands by the window in his dressing gown, holding a square piece of cardboard stained with green smudges. He studies it closely, turning it slightly in the light. The bed in the room remains untouched, its covers smooth and undisturbed.
related_events: Holmes examines cardboard with green smudges
Holmes does not sleep in his bed

name: Holmes Changes for Bed and Recalls a Case in Constantinople
description: In the small, gaslit train compartment, Holmes pulls a nightshirt over his head. Gabrielle's head appears from under the covers of the lower berth. She asks if he is embarrassed, and Holmes replies that he is not, adding that he once spent the night with women during a case in a harem in Constantinople. He then begins to climb the ladder toward the upper berth.
related_events: Holmes pulls night-shirt over his head in train compartment
Gabrielle emerges from under covers of lower berth
Holmes recounts experience in Constantinople harem
Holmes climbs ladder toward upper berth

name: Holmes and Watson Arrive at the Diogenes Club
description: Holmes and Watson climbed the steps of a building with a grand Palladian facade. A discreet sign beside the entrance read: DIOGENES CLUB. Members Only. As they reached the top, Watson paused and voiced his unease about meeting Madame Valladon. Holmes assured him she was safe with Mrs. Hudson. Without further delay, Holmes opened the door, and they stepped inside.
related_events: Holmes and Watson ascend the steps to the Diogenes Club
Watson expresses apprehension about meeting Madame Valladon
Holmes reassures Watson about Madame Valladon's safety
related_occasions: Visit To The Diogenes Club

name: Holmes Changes into Smoking Jacket and Smokes Pipe
description: After the evening's peculiar adventure, Holmes removes his dinner coat and puts on a smoking jacket. He sits down in a wing chair and lights his pipe. The room is quiet, lit only by the desk lamp. Outside, the city sounds fade into the background as he leans back, smoke curling into the air.
related_events: Holmes changes into smoking jacket and smokes pipe after adventure

name: Holmes Recognizes Angry Visitor Approaching
description: Hasty, angry footsteps echoed on the street outside, drawing closer to the house. Holmes, seated in the wing chair in his smoking jacket, turned his head slowly toward the window, his expression calm, as if expecting the visitor all along.
related_events: Angry footsteps approach Holmes's house from the street
Holmes turns head upon recognizing approaching footsteps

name: Holmes and the Parsley in the Butter
description: On a train journey, Watson stirs from a doze and recalls a past case. He remembers how Holmes, during an investigation, examined a dish of butter left in the warmth of a summer day. A sprig of parsley had sunk deep into the softening butter, and by measuring the depth of its submersion, Holmes determined the exact time the butter had been left out. This observation exposed a fatal flaw in the murderer’s alibi, revealing that the man could not have been where he claimed to be at the time of the crime. The memory surfaces quietly, as Holmes sits across the compartment, motionless and silent, his face half-shadowed by the brim of his deerstalker.
related_events: Watson recalls Holmes breaking a murderer's alibi using parsley in butter

name: Holmes and Watson Doze on the Train
description: In a train compartment in 1887, Sherlock Holmes and Dr. John H. Watson sit across from each other by the window, both lightly dozing. Holmes wears a deerstalker and an Inverness cape, while Watson is dressed in a dark overcoat and a black bowler hat, his furled umbrella between his legs and a medical bag beside him on the seat. Their luggage rests on the racks above. The rhythmic motion of the train carries them forward in silence.
related_events: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. John H. Watson doze in a train compartment

name: Watson Ponders Holmes's Feelings on Women
description: A fire crackles in the grate, casting a warm glow over the sitting room. Holmes lies on the couch, his violin in hand, drawing out a series of slow, melancholic variations by Corelli. The music fills the room with a quiet intensity. In his usual armchair, Watson sits reading the Evening Standard, the paper rustling softly as he turns a page. His eyes drift from the text, settling into thought. He wonders about Holmes’s attitude toward women—whether there is a hidden depth beneath his calm logic, or if he is truly a man without emotion. The violin continues, weaving through the silence between them.
related_events: Watson reflects on Holmes's attitude toward women
Watson reads Evening Standard in his usual chair

name: Holmes Plays Corelli on the Violin
description: Holmes lies stretched out on the couch, his violin in hand. The room is still, lit by the glow of a fire in the grate. He draws the bow across the strings, playing a series of variations by Corelli. The music fills the sitting room, soft and measured, as Watson sits nearby in his chair, reading the evening paper.
related_events: Holmes plays Corelli variations on violin while lying on couch

name: Policeman Takes Cover from Watersprinkling Wagon During Patrol
description: The street lamps are still lit. A policeman on patrol walks along the sidewalk, swinging his truncheon. He sees something ahead and, alarmed, quickly steps into the doorway of a building, pressing himself against the door. From the opposite direction, a horse-drawn watersprinkling wagon approaches, spraying water across the street and sidewalks. The policeman remains in the doorway until the wagon passes. Once it is gone, he steps out, relieved, and continues his patrol.
related_events: Policeman notices something alarming during patrol
Policeman takes cover in a building doorway
Horse-drawn watersprinkling wagon sprays street and sidewalks
Policeman resumes patrol after wagon passes

name: Holmes and Watson Return to 221B
description: A hansom cab pulls up in front of 221B Baker Street, carrying Holmes and Watson. The driver begins unloading their luggage from the roof of the cab. Mrs. Hudson, wearing an apron, comes out of the building and hurries down the steps to greet them. She welcomes the two men warmly. Holmes, Watson, and Mrs. Hudson then go inside the house as the cabbie continues to handle their belongings.
related_events: Hansom cab arrives at 221B Baker Street with Holmes and Watson
Mrs. Hudson greets Holmes and Watson at the door
Cabbie unloads luggage from the hansom cab
Holmes, Watson, and Mrs. Hudson enter 221B Baker Street

name: Gabrielle Found in Holmes' Bed
description: Watson stood in the doorway of Holmes' room, looking inside. Mrs. Hudson came up behind him and peered over his shoulder. On the bed, Gabrielle lay asleep, covered only by a sheet, clearly naked beneath. Mrs. Hudson drew in a sharp breath and said, 'Well, I never!' Just then, the sound of the front door opening came from the hall, and both of them turned toward the noise.
related_events: Mrs. Hudson peers over Watson's shoulder in the doorway
Mrs. Hudson expresses shock at seeing Gabrielle in Holmes' bed

name: Watson and Mrs. Hudson Turn at the Sound of the Door
description: The front door opened with a distinct creak, drawing the attention of Watson and Mrs. Hudson. Both turned their heads toward the entrance, their focus shifting from the bedroom to the sound in the hall.
related_events: Hall door opens and Watson and Mrs. Hudson turn toward the sound

name: Holmes Arranges the Room Before Watson Returns
description: Holmes stands up, turns the wing chair so that its back faces the door, walks to the desk lamp, and turns the wick down. From outside comes the sound of a key turning in the front door lock. The door opens, and Watson steps into the vestibule, then hurries up the stairs and across the landing. He throws open the door to the flat and calls out Holmes's name.
related_events: Holmes adjusts chair and dims lamp

name: Watson Returns and Confronts Holmes
description: Watson arrives at 221B Baker Street, unlocks the front door, and strides into the vestibule. He climbs the stairs quickly, crosses the landing, and flings the flat door open. Standing in the doorway, he calls out, 'Holmes!'
related_events: Watson returns to 221B Baker Street
Watson enters Holmes's flat in urgency

name: Arrival at the Hotel
description: An open carriage moves along the driveway toward the hotel, its approach scattering a flock of sheep grazing nearby. Watson sits beside the coachman, while Holmes and Gabrielle occupy the passenger seat, their luggage secured at the back. Through the trees lining the road, Loch Ness is visible, partially shrouded in low-lying mist. The carriage draws up in front of the hotel, coming to a stop beneath the sign above the entrance. Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle step out onto the ground. Inside, a close shot shows a hand writing in the hotel register: Mr. And Mrs. Ashdown and valet, London.
related_events: Carriage travels toward hotel and scatters grazing sheep
Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle arrive at hotel entrance
Holmes, Watson, and Gabrielle disembark from carriage

name: Holmes Registers as Mr. and Mrs. Ashdown
description: The carriage rolls to a stop in front of the hotel, scattering a flock of sheep grazing near the driveway. Watson climbs down from the seat beside the coachman, followed by Holmes and Gabrielle. Their luggage remains strapped to the back of the carriage. Holmes steps into the hotel and approaches the register. His hand moves across the page, writing: Mr. And Mrs. Ashdown and valet, London.
related_events: Holmes registers at hotel under assumed names

name: Monk Confirms Watson Is Asleep and Whispers to Another Monk
description: The monk seated beside Watson watches him closely until he is certain Watson has fallen asleep. He then quietly rises and moves toward another monk sitting apart from the others. Leaning in, he whispers, 'Die Spur führt nach Inverness. Die steigen dort aus. Dort müssen wir ihn finden – den Valladon!' The other monk looks up, his face revealed under the cowl as von Tirpitz.
related_events: Monk confirms Watson is asleep before moving
Monk rises and approaches another monk seated apart

name: Monk Whispers Mission to von Tirpitz in Disguise
description: One of the monks, seated beside Watson, waits until the others have fallen asleep in their seats. He quietly rises and moves toward another monk sitting apart. Leaning in, he whispers in German, 'Die Spur führt nach Inverness. Die steigen dort aus. Dort müssen wir ihn finden – den Valladon!' The monk addressed slowly looks up, lowering his cowl to reveal the face of von Tirpitz.
related_events: Monk whispers plan to von Tirpitz about tracking Valladon
Von Tirpitz revealed under cowl of monk's robe

name: Holmes Watches Gabrielle and Leaves
description: Holmes slowly opens the door and looks into the room, where Gabrielle lies asleep in Watson's bed. He stands quietly, watching her for a moment. Then, without making a sound, he pulls the door shut. The latch clicks into place.
related_events: Holmes observes Gabrielle sleeping in Watson's bed
Holmes quietly closes the door after observing Gabrielle

name: Gabrielle Awakens and Calls Out
description: The click of the latch closing startles Gabrielle awake. She sits up in bed, her back to the room, and turns slightly as she calls out, 'Emile?' Reaching to get out of bed, she moves as if responding to someone she believes is present.
related_events: Gabrielle awakens and sits up in bed
Gabrielle calls out and begins to get out of bed

name: Von Tirpitz Signals the Start of the Pursuit
description: From inside a parked hansom across the street, von Tirpitz watches Gabrielle at the upstairs window of 221B. She closes her parasol and moves away. Von Tirpitz raises his hand in a clear signal. The cabbie, perched at the front, flicks the whip. The horse surges forward, and the hansom rolls away from the curb, turning to follow the street in the direction of Gabrielle’s building.
related_events: Von Tirpitz signals the cabbie from across the street
Cabbie whips the horse to start the hansom moving

name: Gabrielle Closes Her Parasol at the Window
description: Gabrielle stands at the upstairs window of 221B and shuts her parasol. From across the street, von Tirpitz watches. He signals to the cabbie, who flicks his whip and drives the hansom down the street.
related_events: Gabrielle closes the parasol at 221B window

name: Hansom Cab Arrives with Mysterious Woman Passenger
description: A hansom cab emerges from the swirling fog and rolls to a stop in front of 221B Baker Street. A woman sits inside, her figure barely visible in the dim light. The driver climbs down from his seat, moving slowly in the damp air. Above, the faint sound of a violin drifts from an upper window.
related_events: Hansom cab arrives at 221B Baker Street
Woman passenger visible in hansom cab
Cab driver begins to dismount from vehicle

name: Violin Music from 221B
description: Faint strains of violin music drift down from the upstairs apartment at 221B Baker Street. The sound mingles with the still night air, carrying through the fog that clings to the street below.
related_events: Violin music plays from upstairs apartment

name: Watson Pleads with Holmes to Attend the Ballet
description: Watson finishes his coffee, picks up a letter on blue note-paper and a pair of theatre tickets, and walks toward Holmes's bedroom. Inside, Holmes sits in a hip-bath, soaping himself. Watson stands in the doorway and urges him to go to the final performance of the Imperial Russian Ballet, pointing out that the house has been sold out for months and the seats are now going for a guinea apiece. He reads from the letter: 'Please! You are the only man in the world who can help me.' Holmes remains skeptical, questioning why someone would send two free tickets anonymously. Watson insists the sender must be in great distress, but Holmes declares his detestation of ballet, calling the invitation a plot to bore him to death.
related_events: Watson finishes coffee and prepares to confront Holmes
Watson delivers frustrated appeal to Holmes about attending the ballet
Holmes remains in hip-bath while Watson confronts him
related_occasions: Final Performance Of The Imperial Russian Ballet

name: Holmes and Watson Argue Over Anonymous Ballet Tickets
description: Watson finishes his coffee at the table, holding a letter on blue note-paper and a pair of theatre tickets. He picks them up and begins to pace toward Holmes's bedroom. Inside, Holmes sits in a hip-bath, soaping himself. Watson stands in the doorway, urging Holmes to accept the tickets to the final performance of the Imperial Russian Ballet. He mentions the show is sold out and seats are going for a guinea each. Holmes questions why anyone would send two free tickets anonymously. Watson reads from the note: 'Please! You are the only man in the world who can help me,' and suggests the sender is in great distress. Holmes remains skeptical, suspecting a trap. Watson asks if someone might be trying to kill him. Holmes replies that someone is trying to kill him by boring him to death, confessing his detestation of ballet. Watson counters that it is not just any ballet—it is Swan Lake.
related_events: Holmes expresses suspicion about the origin of the theatre tickets
Watson interprets the note as a plea from someone in distress
Holmes reveals his fear of being bored to death at the ballet
related_occasions: Final Performance Of The Imperial Russian Ballet
Performance Of Swan Lake By The Imperial Russian Ballet

name: Holmes and Watson Ignore the Porter and Head Upstairs
description: Holmes and Watson enter the lobby of the Diogenes Club, where a one-armed porter in uniform stands behind the reception desk. The porter opens a leather-bound register, turns it toward them, and begins to ask for their details. Before he can finish, Holmes and Watson turn and walk toward the grand staircase. The porter watches in surprise as they climb the steps without signing in. He steps out from behind the desk and calls after them, but they do not stop.
related_events: Holmes and Watson enter the building lobby
Porter offers visitor registration form to Holmes and Watson
Holmes and Watson ignore registration and ascend the staircase
Porter reacts to Holmes and Watson leaving

name: Holmes Examines Cigar Ash in the Reading Room
description: Holmes and Watson walk through the Diogenes Club's reading room toward the study. As they pass, Holmes notices a sleeping club member with a long ash clinging to the end of his lit cigar. Holmes picks up an ashtray, holds it beneath the cigar just as the ash begins to fall, and catches it. He studies the ash closely, then remarks that the tobacco is Jamaican, either Tropical or Golosina, before continuing on with Watson.
related_events: Holmes observes sleeping club member with long ash on cigar
Holmes catches cigar ash with ashtray to examine it
Holmes identifies cigar ash as Jamaican tobacco
related_occasions: Diogenes Club Reading Room Gathering

name: Von Tirpitz Boards the Moving Hansom
description: A man steps out of the fog into the circle of light beneath a streetlamp. His face is craggy, weathered, about fifty years old. He looks up toward the windows of the Holmes flat. At that moment, a hansom cab completes a U-turn and moves past him. As it passes, the man quickly hops into the cab and disappears inside. The cab continues forward, swallowed by the fog.
related_events: Von Tirpitz steps out of fog into streetlamp light
Von Tirpitz looks up toward Holmes flat
Von Tirpitz hops into moving hansom cab

name: Cabbie Readies the Hansom Cab
description: The cabbie tossed a blanket into the hansom and climbed onto the driver's seat. As the cab made a U-turn, a man stepped out of the fog into the circle of light beneath a street lamp. He was a craggy-faced Prussian of about fifty, dressed in a long coat, and he looked up toward the Holmes flat. The cab drew alongside him, and he climbed in. It pulled away and vanished into the fog.
related_events: Cabbie tosses blanket into hansom and mounts driver's seat

name: Von Tirpitz Enters the Hansom Cab
description: The cabbie tossed the blanket into the hansom and climbed onto the driver's seat. A man stepped out of the fog across the street, emerging into the circle of light beneath a street lamp. He was a craggy-faced Prussian of about fifty, named Von Tirpitz. He looked up toward the Holmes flat. As the hansom made a U-turn and drew alongside him, he climbed in. The cab continued forward and disappeared into the fog.
related_events: Hansom cab disappears into fog

name: Watson Retrieves His Hat and Umbrella
description: Watson enters the carriage and makes his way down the aisle toward a window seat where he has left his umbrella and bowler hat. The seat is occupied by monks in brown habits, with more monks on the bench across from them. As Watson squeezes between them to reach his belongings, he steps on one monk's foot. He picks up his bowler and umbrella, then settles into the seat.
related_events: Watson retrieves his bowler hat and umbrella from the window seat
Watson steps on a monk's foot while squeezing through the aisle

name: Watson Attempts Conversation with a Silent Monk
description: After settling into his seat, Watson turns to the monk beside him and asks if the monks are going to Scotland, mentioning that he and his master and mistress are also traveling to Inverness. He comments on the beauty of the country and explains that he works as a valet. The monk looks up from his Bible, points to his lips, and shakes his head. Watson apologizes, assuming the monk belongs to an order that has taken a vow of silence, specifically the Trappists. The monk does not respond. Watson then turns away, pulls down the window shade, and closes his eyes.
related_events: Watson attempts to engage a monk in conversation
Watson reveals he is a valet while conversing with a monk
Monk silently indicates he cannot speak
Watson misinterprets monk's silence and identifies it as Trappist vow

name: Watson Notices the Book of Jonah and Falls Silent
description: Watson glances at the Bible in the monk's hands and sees that it is open to the Book of Jonah. 'I see you're reading the book of Jonah,' he says. 'Funny—we were just talking about Johan this morning.' He pauses, then stops speaking. He pulls down the window shade, closes his eyes, and sits quietly, no longer attempting to engage.
related_events: Watson notices the Bible is open to the Book of Jonah
Watson abandons conversation and attempts to sleep

name: Mrs. Hudson Wakes Watson and Helps Him Rise
description: Mrs. Hudson opened the curtains, letting sunlight flood the room. She walked over to the couch where Watson was lying and clapped her hands. Dr. Watson! Your porridge is getting lumpy. Hadn't you better get up? Watson tried to rise but fell back with a moan. I would like to very much. But — he turned onto his stomach. Mrs. Hudson, would you mind planting your knee in the small of my back? Yes, I would, she replied. Please! I'm in excruciating pain. Hesitantly, Mrs. Hudson placed her knee on his back. A bit higher — just below my seventh vertebra — he guided. She adjusted. Put your arms under mine — fold them behind my neck. She pressed down, and a distinct snap sounded. Bless you, Watson said as he sat up, rubbing his neck. That damn couch. He walked to the table and sat. You'd better see if our patient is awake, he said. Mrs. Hudson went to the door of Watson's bedroom, opened it, and stopped. Dr. Watson. She's gone. Watson jumped up and joined her. The bed was empty. Gabrielle's clothes were still there, but she was not. Watson strode toward Holmes' bedroom, threw the door open, and froze in the doorway.
related_events: Mrs. Hudson opens curtains and wakes Watson for breakfast
Watson requests help to relieve back pain
Mrs. Hudson assists Watson with spinal adjustment
Watson rises and complains about the couch
Watson sits down to breakfast and suggests checking on the patient

name: Watson Discovers Gabrielle Missing and Reacts to a Shock in Holmes' Room
description: Mrs. Hudson opens the door to Gabrielle's bedroom and stops suddenly, announcing that Gabrielle is gone. Watson leaps up from the breakfast table and rushes to the room, seeing the empty bed with Gabrielle's clothes still there. He immediately strides toward Holmes' bedroom, calling out as he throws the door open. He steps forward but freezes in place, his eyes fixed on something inside the room.
related_events: Mrs. Hudson discovers Gabrielle is missing from her bedroom
Watson reacts to news of Gabrielle's disappearance
Watson rushes to Holmes' bedroom to report Gabrielle's disappearance
Watson freezes upon seeing something in Holmes' bedroom

name: Holmes Pries Open the Coffin
description: Holmes stands in a large grave from which the earth has been dug away. He drives the point of a crowbar under the edge of a coffin lid, forcing it upward. The lid resists, then gives with a squeal of straining nails. Watson and Gabrielle kneel at the edge of the grave, watching. Watson holds a bullseye lantern. The coffin opens to reveal the body of Emile Valladon, a middle-aged man with arms folded across his chest. A wedding ring, similar to Gabrielle's, glints on the third finger of his left hand. Gabrielle lets out a piercing scream and collapses. Watson catches her before she falls. Holmes takes the lantern from Watson and lowers it into the coffin. The light moves along the body, revealing three canaries at Valladon's feet—small birds with plumage bleached a lifeless grey-white.
related_events: Holmes pries open coffin lid with a crowbar
Corpse of Emile Valladon revealed in coffin

name: Gabrielle Recognizes Valladon and Faints
description: The coffin lid creaks open under Holmes's crowbar, revealing the body of a middle-aged man with arms crossed over his chest. Gabrielle stares at the face, then lets out a piercing scream. She collapses, and Watson catches her before she hits the ground.
related_events: Gabrielle identifies Emile Valladon's body and faints
Watson catches collapsing Gabrielle

name: Holmes Examines the Corpse in the Coffin
description: Holmes takes the bullseye lantern from Watson and directs the beam into the open coffin. He studies the body of Emile Valladon, noting the green discoloration on the wedding ring adorning the third finger of the corpse's left hand. The light moves downward, revealing three canaries lying at the feet of the body, their feathers bleached a pale, lifeless white.
related_events: Holmes examines coffin with bullseye lantern beam
Holmes observes green discoloration on Valladon's wedding ring
Holmes discovers three bleached white canaries in the coffin

name: Holmes and Watson Return to Find Mrs. Hudson on Guard
description: Mrs. Hudson opened the door holding a gun in one hand and an embroidery hoop in the other. She had unhooked the chain and stepped aside as Holmes and Watson entered the vestibule. Holmes took the gun from her and noted it was not loaded. Without pause, he started up the stairs, Watson following behind.
related_events: Mrs. Hudson opens the door after holding a gun and embroidery hoop
Holmes and Watson enter the vestibule after being admitted by Mrs. Hudson
Holmes takes the unloaded gun from Mrs. Hudson

name: Holmes and Watson Return to the Flat
description: Holmes and Watson climb the stairs to their flat. As they ascend, Watson asks Holmes whether he intends to disobey Mycroft's orders, reminding him that Mycroft is not only his brother but a representative of the government. Holmes does not respond. Upon reaching the landing, they find Gabrielle waiting for them in the open doorway of their flat.
related_events: Holmes and Watson arrive at the landing outside their flat

name: Holmes and Watson Return to the Flat
description: Holmes and Watson ascend the stairs and reach the landing outside their flat. Gabrielle stands in the open doorway, waiting for them. She steps forward and asks if they have any news or have found out anything.
related_events: Holmes and Watson arrive at the landing outside their flat
Gabrielle greets Holmes and Watson at the doorway of the flat

name: Gabrielle Mistakes Holmes for Emile
description: Gabrielle steps out of Watson's bedroom and looks around. She sees Holmes and calls out, 'Emile? Is that you, Emile?' Holmes steps into the shadow and answers. She hurries toward him, embraces him tightly, and says, 'Hold me. Hold me tight. It's been such a long time. So many nights.' She tells him about buying a pink negligee with maribou feathers before leaving Brussels and asks if he thinks it's foolish for a married woman. Then she moves toward the bed, gets in, and beckons him to join her.
related_events: Gabrielle exits Watson's bedroom and approaches Holmes
Holmes responds to Gabrielle while stepping into shadow
Gabrielle embraces Holmes and expresses longing
Holmes physically comforts Gabrielle

name: Gabrielle Confesses About the Pink Negligee
description: Believing Holmes to be Emile, Gabrielle steps out of Watson's bedroom and hurries toward him, calling his name. She embraces him tightly, saying it has been too long. She confesses that before leaving Brussels, she bought herself an expensive pink negligee with maribou feathers, and wonders aloud if that is foolish for a married woman. Then she moves to the bed, gets in, and beckons him to join her, extending her hand. Holmes approaches, asking where the negligee is. She tells him it is in her luggage, though she does not know its location, and pleads with him to come to her.
related_events: Gabrielle reveals she bought a pink negligee in Brussels
Gabrielle gets into bed and beckons Holmes to join her

name: Holmes Finds a Hidden Number on Gabrielle's Palm
description: As Gabrielle reached out to Holmes, he noticed faint marks on the palm of her hand—letters in green ink that matched the smudges on the cardboard. Without a word, he turned to the wash-stand, picked up a small magnifying mirror, and returned to the bed. Holding the mirror against her palm, he studied the reflection. The markings, reversed in the glass, formed the number '301'. Gabrielle watched, puzzled. 'What is it, Emile? What are you doing?' she asked, but Holmes remained silent, focused on the clue now revealed.
related_events: Holmes notices green ink letters on Gabrielle's palm
Holmes uses magnifying mirror to examine handwriting on Gabrielle's palm
Mirror reveals hidden number '301' on Gabrielle's palm
Gabrielle questions Holmes about his investigative actions

name: Holmes and Gabrielle Discuss Women on the Train
description: Gabrielle lies in the lower berth, reading a copy of Strand Magazine by the light of a gas lamp, with other magazines scattered around her. From the upper berth, shrouded in darkness, Holmes calls down after hearing her speak. She remarks that women are never to be trusted entirely, then clarifies she was quoting something attributed to him in the magazine by Dr. Watson. Holmes protests that Watson often puts words in his mouth, but does not deny the sentiment. Instead, he agrees that he is not a whole-hearted admirer of womankind. Gabrielle offers a sympathetic response, but Holmes insists his view is shaped by personal experience, not just professional encounters with criminals. He recalls his fiancée, the daughter of his violin teacher, who died of influenza one day before their wedding, and uses the memory to reaffirm his belief in women's unreliability. After a pause, he bids her good night. She returns the greeting, and each draws the curtain of their berth as the train whistle sounds.
related_events: Gabrielle reads Strand Magazine in lower berth by gas lamp light
Holmes questions Gabrielle about her comment on women
Gabrielle attributes quote to Holmes via Dr. Watson
Holmes denies authorship but confirms skepticism toward women

name: Holmes Recounts a Murderous Affair and a Lost Engagement
description: Holmes lies in the upper berth as Gabrielle reads below by the light of a gas lamp. She comments on a quote attributed to him about women being untrustworthy. Holmes acknowledges he did not say it, but does not deny the sentiment. He describes a past affair with a woman he knew who was a murderess, recalling that their meetings took place in his laboratory and that she stole cyanide there to poison her husband. Gabrielle objects, but Holmes insists he judges only the women he has been involved with, not just as clients but personally. He then speaks of his former fiancée, the daughter of his violin teacher, with whom he had planned to marry. The wedding invitations were sent, and he was being fitted for a tailcoat when she died of influenza one day before the wedding. After a pause, he bids Gabrielle good night, and she returns the wish as he draws the curtain of his berth and the train whistle sounds.
related_events: Holmes recounts affair with murderess in laboratory
Holmes reveals engagement to daughter of violin teacher
Holmes attributes fiancée's death to influenza

name: Holmes and Gabrielle End Their Conversation
description: After recounting the story of his fiancée's sudden death, Holmes states that women are unreliable and not to be trusted. He then says, 'Good night, Mrs. Ashdown,' and pulls the curtain shut around his upper berth. Gabrielle replies, 'Good night, Mr. Ashdown,' and closes her own curtain as the train whistle blows.
related_events: Holmes concludes women are untrustworthy based on personal experience
Holmes bids good night to Gabrielle and draws berth curtain
Gabrielle returns good night and closes her berth curtain

name: Packing Watson's Belongings and Saying Goodbye
description: Two valises lie open on the bed. Watson moves about the room, collecting personal items, while Mrs. Hudson folds his clothes and places them into one of the bags. She pauses, overcome, and wipes her eyes. Watson approaches her gently, urging her not to be upset. She takes a handkerchief from the valise, blows her nose, and says she will wash it and send it to him. Watson tells her he will be staying at Brown's Hotel. He recalls seeing something himself on Easter Sunday, but trails off, saying no one listens. Holmes gives him a few coins. The man thanks them, warns them to avoid Loch Ness, and leaves with his partner, shovels over their shoulders. Watson scoffs at the tale. name: The Venice Conception Proposal
description: Petrova, seated at her dressing table, turned to Rogozhin and asked through him what time they would be leaving for Venice. Rogozhin replied that all arrangements had been made for a week-long trip, just the two of them, for the purpose of conceiving a child. He added that several men had been considered before Holmes—among them Tchaikovsky—but each had been dismissed for one reason or another. Tchaikovsky, he explained, showed no interest in women at all. Petrova smiled, then looked Holmes directly in the eye, expressing her satisfaction with him as the chosen partner. Holmes hesitated, citing the emotional reserve typical of Englishmen and his family’s history of hemophilia. Rogozhin assured him the arrangement was strictly practical, not romantic. Petrova, noticing his concern, held up her hands and said calmly that she would not scratch him—her nails were perfectly smooth. She then asked why he seemed reluctant, questioning whether he found her unattractive. Holmes, after a pause, explained that he lived with Dr. Watson and considered their bond a domestic partnership. Rogozhin, with a knowing look, interpreted this as a romantic union, but made no objection. The terms were understood. The journey to Venice was confirmed.

name: Watson's Night at the Ball
description: After Holmes left the party, Watson continued dancing, moving joyfully among the ballerinas, his laughter blending with the music. He spun and leapt with one partner after another, caught in the glow of the celebration. Rogozhin watched from the edge of the room, his expression darkening as he observed Watson’s exuberance. He drew close to a group of dancers, leaned in, and whispered something in low tones. The ballerinas exchanged glances, then slowly began to withdraw from Watson. One by one, they found other partners, leaving him momentarily alone on the floor. When the next dance began, male dancers approached him instead, guiding him into the rhythm without explanation. Watson danced on, at first unaware, then increasingly unsettled. He looked around, noticing the absence of the women who had welcomed him moments before. His steps faltered. He made his way to Rogozhin, who stood with a faint smirk, swirling his drink. Watson confronted him, voice rising over the music. Rogozhin only gestured vaguely toward a slender figure in the distance—Sergei—then murmured that Holmes had already been informed about Watson’s relationship. Without another word, Watson seized Rogozhin’s glass of vodka and drank it down.
